results.title: 😸 Thirty windows, one button | Product Hunt
results.content:
Captain Kill Switch is one button in your menu bar that closes every running app. Simon Crean built it after the same stupid moment kept repeating, finishing for the day with thirty-odd windows open and shutting them one at a time, which he describes as tidying a room by picking up individual grains of rice. No dashboard, no settings, no account. Anything still open a couple of seconds later gets force-closed, unsaved work and all, and he says that on the launch page rather than letting you find out on a Friday evening, which is the right way round.

LinkFlick — Stop re-pairing your Magic Keyboard between Macs [...] SurveyMonkey — Your best decisions start with listening

SurveyMonkey now asks your customers questions in conversation, the way a person actually would, and hands the answers back already analysed. Nobody fills in a grid of radio buttons voluntarily. It benchmarks your numbers against companies in your space, so you find out whether your score is good or quietly terrible, and it plugs into ChatGPT and Slack so the feedback lands where you already argue about things, with no research team to hire and no fieldwork to wait on.

results.title: I just hit the kill switch on my own app… : Self-Promotion Discussion Forums | Product Hunt
results.content:
Title: I just hit the kill switch on my own app… : Self-Promotion Discussion Forums | Product Hunt
### Topic Forums. ### Product Forums. Studio – Your AI Media Copilot. # I just hit the kill switch on my own app…. **🚀 Road to 1,000,000 #Votap users — Day 65 | Current: 1348**. **I just hit the kill switch on my own app…**. And honestly… every app should have this. Right after pushing the new update, I wanted to test it like a normal user. Very soon I spotted a bug. Because of a concurrency issue, some users who already had a username assigned could sometimes see the picker again… and sometimes not. That’s the worst kind of bug. Pure “luck” depending on what runs first. So I didn’t risk it. **I flipped the app into maintenance mode**. Everyone sees a simple screen, no interaction, until it’s fixed. Not fun… but way better than letting users run into broken logic. I always knew I’d mess something up eventually 🤣. This time it was concurrency. If you’re building an app — have a kill switch. You’ll thank yourself later. Fix is already in app review.
